verdicts.flaw_description: The reported purchase counts "cover the sessions that reached the new page" while "a quarter of each segment dropped out before checkout", so the 4-7 percent gains are computed on a self-selected 75 percent of each segment rather than the whole segment the claim is about. The site-wide discount is neutralised (fixed-price contract catalogue), but the population mismatch is not.

"The figures cover the runs with the upgraded filter in service, and a quarter of each stack's runs were made with the filter bypassed" - so the 8-14 percent reductions are measured on only three quarters of each stack's runs, a narrower set than the earlier-quarter baseline they are compared against, and narrower than the stack-level readings the claim concerns.

"Averages cover the patients who kept up the home exercises, and a quarter of each intake let the home exercises lapse" - the 9-16 degree gains are averaged over only the adherent three quarters of each intake, selecting on post-treatment behaviour, so they do not show what the protocol did for the intake as a whole.

"Rates cover the trays sown from seed that took a full coat, and about a fifth of each lot's trays were sown from partly coated seed" - the 6-11 point germination gains exclude roughly a fifth of each lot, and seed that takes a full coat may differ in quality from seed that does not, so the figures describe a narrower and non-random subset of the lot.

"Pass rates cover the students who attended every block, and about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block" - the 4-8 point gains are computed only on full attenders, dropping about a quarter of each cohort, so the comparison against the previous spring term is against a differently constituted (and self-selected) group.
